checks: Same-parity midpoint bases are integral and the actual Minkowski inclusion gives positive d-volume and the stated Brunn–Minkowski inequality.

At a nonmaximizing base the volume strictly increases. At an unchosen maximizing tie the squared norm strictly drops if the volume does not increase, by the exact polarization identity and the tie rule. This proves finite descent to the fixed roots without requiring all classes.
Solving F(z)=y within a class gives at most one preimage. Iterating the Minkowski midpoint inclusions assigns the initial coefficient 2^−k and coefficient 2^(j−k) to root j.

The binomial difference is nondecreasing in its initial argument for t≥0. This yields the absolute coefficient 2^−d. The actual three-fiber affine-homothetic example tends to this ratio as s decreases, while all included fibers remain positive for s>0.
Source 59540588b70a065b §2 (6)–(10) uses volume-maximizing occupied roots with the same tie rule and says nothing about a disjoint transport of the arriving copies.

overlap.comparison: It gives termination and dyadic transport under the additional assumption that the designated root hull has no other integer sites. The present termination uses lexicographic volume/norm descent and adds the sharp quantitative volume growth.
It assumes the homothetic forest terminates and its edges are exact Minkowski equalities, to derive terminal face patches. Neither assumption is needed for the present descent.
